title: Path Traversal via scala.io.Source
platform_conditions: Scala 2.13 / Scala 3 standard library (scala.io.Source) on the JVM; URL handlers follow JVM protocol resolution
security_mechanism: scala.io.Source.fromURL accepts any java.net.URL-legal scheme, so an attacker-supplied 'file:///etc/passwd' or 'http://169.254.169.254/...' string makes the read API itself the SSRF/local-file primitive -- no separate network call is needed and the content comes back through the same return value. fromFile with a traversal path ('../../..') escapes the intended directory because Source performs no confinement check, and archive entry names carrying absolute paths or '..' do the same at extraction time via JVM file APIs.

source_sink_clues.source: Path or URL strings from requests, import/export parameters, and archive member names.
source_sink_clues.sink: scala.io.Source.fromURL / fromFile over attacker-influenced strings; JVM File/Paths operations over archive entry names

tracking_guards: Check URL reads restrict the scheme to an allowlist and the host to a validated set resolved before the request; check file reads normalize the candidate and verify containment under the base directory (startsWith on canonical paths); check archive entry names reject absolute paths and '..' segments.
not_candidate_when: The path is generated server-side, a canonical-path containment check rejects escapes before reading, or the URL is restricted to an allowlisted scheme+host with redirects disabled.
public_references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
OWASP Server Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
